Security Headers with Helmet

helmet() sets over a dozen safe-default response headers in one line — registered first, so every response gets them.

A browser's own behaviour is steered by a handful of HTTP response headers most APIs never think to set — whether a page can be embedded in an <iframe> (clickjacking), whether the browser should try to guess a response's content type instead of trusting the one it was given (MIME-sniffing), whether the X-Powered-By: Express header should announce exactly which framework and version an attacker is dealing with. None of this is specific to the Support Desk domain — it's the same handful of headers any Express API should set — which is exactly what the helmet package exists to do:

// Figure 6.14: registered first, in app.js
import helmet from 'helmet';

const app = express();

app.use(helmet());
app.use(cors());
// ...

helmet() is a bundle of more than a dozen smaller middleware functions, each setting one header, with reasonable defaults for a JSON API — it's registered before anything else in app.js precisely so every response this API ever sends, success or error, carries them. There's no Support-Desk-specific configuration here: this is the one middleware in this lesson that's genuinely "add the package, call it, done."
